claim_a_text: Two-stage detectors like Faster R-CNN are state-of-the-art and achieve high accuracy by using region proposals to filter out most background samples.
claim_b_text: One-stage detectors like RetinaNet can match or surpass the accuracy of two-stage detectors when trained with focal loss, eliminating the accuracy gap.
claim_a_quote: State-of-the-art object detection networks depend on region proposal algorithms to hypothesize object locations.
claim_b_quote: Our results show that when trained with the focal loss, RetinaNet is able to match the speed of previous one-stage detectors while surpassing the accuracy of all existing state-of-the-art two-stage detectors.
rationale: ARTICLE_A presents the two-stage Faster R-CNN as the state-of-the-art foundation for high accuracy, while ARTICLE_B claims that its one-stage RetinaNet with focal loss surpasses the accuracy of all existing two-stage detectors, indicating a shift in the leading paradigm.
